LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#19 Travel with Me Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 2: sets of Memory cards 
(P.4.2 + P.4.7) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: Country flash cards 
(P.4.3) + paper airplanes 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Country flash cards 
(P.4.3) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Country flash cards 
(P.4.3)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 7: Country Bingo boards + 
Attraction cards (P.4.7) + counters
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game 
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game Reference Sheet 
•	 Dice and Counters (1 per child) 
BEFORE CLASS
If it’s the last day of the story, check the teacher’s dashboard 
to see if the Ss have completed Mission 4.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (10’) 
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Calendar
•	 After-School Activities
•	 My Pet

2.– STORY QUESTIONS (10’)
There will not be any storytelling in today’s lesson, students 
will work on the story in a more fun way. The students will be 
asked questions about the story and will be expected to give 
the appropriate answers. You can bring along some props like 
a bandana or buzzer to make it even more fun. 
Suggested questions are as follows:
•	 What are Pam, Paul and Grandma doing at the 
beginning of the story? They are cleaning the attic.
•	 What did Paul see in the attic? Paul saw a big brown 
suitcase.
•	 What was there inside the suitcase? There was a 
(very old-looking) glass bottle.
•	 What was there inside the bottle? There was a genie.
•	 What did Grandma visit in the United States of 
America? Grandma visited the Statue of Liberty (in 
New York City).
•	 What did Grandma see in Australia? Grandma saw 
the kangaroos in Australia.
•	 What did the genie do? He granted Pam and Paul 
three wishes.
•	 What did they ask for? They asked to travel to Australia, 
Egypt and China.
•	 What did they visit in China? They visited the Great 
Wall in China.
Please, note that these are only suggestions. You might want 
to expand them if you deem necessary.
3.– ACTIVITY 2: WHERE DID THEY GO? (9’)
P.4.2
P.4.2
Egypt
P.4.7
> How to Play
In this activity Ss will create sentences about the characters 
going to different countries and visiting different monuments.

> Warm-Up
Prepare three piles of cards face down, one with characters 
(P.4.2), one with countries (P.4.2) and the other with monuments, 
animals and food (P.4.7). Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s 
find out where the characters travelled to last year!”. Model the 
activity for the Ss by drawing a card from each pile. If possible, 
model both a correct and an incorrect combination of cards.
For example:
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and Mount Fuji from each pile, and 
say, “Pam didn’t go to Egypt to visit Mount Fuji; she 
went to Japan to visit Mount Fuji.”
•	 Take Pam, Egypt and the Pyramids, and say, “Pam 
went to Egypt to visit the pyramids.”
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Ss take a card from each pile and identify whether the 
character went to the right country to visit the monument.
If, for example, they take Dad, India and Taj Mahal, they should 
form a sentence using the following structure: “Dad went to 
India to visit the Taj Mahal.” 
If they don’t find a match, they will have to state the correct 
activity for that country. For example, if a S takes Mum, South 
Africa and Taj Mahal, they will say, “Mum didn’t go to South 
Africa to visit the Taj Mahal; she went to South Africa to see 
the elephants.”. 
You can use prompts and actions where necessary if the Ss 
are unable to remember the different countries and monuments.
NOTE: to play this activity, it is not necessary to consider 
the actual places that the characters visited in the story. For 
cards with food items, you should change the target language 
accordingly “Mum didn’t go to China to eat curry, Mum went 
to India to eat curry.”. Same goes for “go on a safari”, “have a 
barbecue”, “eat noodles”, etc. 
> Follow-Up
Once every S has had a turn, take a correct combination of 
cards and ask the Ss, “Where did Grandma go to and what did 
she do there?” to which the Ss should reply, “Grandma went 
to India to visit the Taj Mahal.” 
Then, show an incorrect combination and ask, “Did Grandma 
go to South Africa to visit the Taj Mahal?” to which Ss should 
reply, “No, she didn’t. She went to India to visit the Taj Mahal.”

4.– ACTIVITY 3: A TRIP AROUND THE WORLD (9’)
P.4.3
Italy
TARGET LANGUAGE
•	 Argentina: in this country people speak Spanish, you 
can have barbecues, and you can visit Patagonia.
•	 Australia: in this country people speak English, you 
can see kangaroos and visit the Great Barrier Reef.
•	 Brazil: in this country people speak Portuguese, you 
can visit Christ the Redeemer and go to the Amazon 
rainforest. 
•	 Canada: in this country people speak English and 
French; you can see polar bears and you can eat maple 
syrup.
•	 China: in this country people speak Chinese, you can 
eat noodles, and you can visit the Great Wall.
•	 Egypt: in this country people speak Arabic, you can 
visit the pyramids and the River Nile.
•	 England: in this country people speak English, you can 
visit Big Ben and the London Eye and it’s very rainy.
•	 France: in this country people speak French, you can 
eat cheese, and you can visit the Eiffel Tower or the 
Louvre Museum.
•	 Germany: in this country people speak German, you 
can eat sausages, and you can visit the Berlin Wall or 
go to the Black Forest.
•	 India: in this country people speak Hindi and English; 
you can eat curry, and you can visit the Taj Mahal.
•	 Italy: in this country people speak Italian, you can eat 
pizza, and you can visit the Colosseum or the Leaning 
Tower of Pisa.
•	 Japan: in this country people speak Japanese, you can 
visit Mount Fuji and many temples.
•	 Madagascar: in this country people speak Malagasy 
and French; you can see lemurs and baobab trees. 
•	 South Africa: in this country people speak English, you 
can see elephants and you can go on a safari.
•	 Spain: in this country people speak Spanish, you can 
visit the Sagrada Familia and the Alhambra.

•	 United States: in this country people speak English, you 
can visit the Grand Canyon and the Statue of Liberty.
> How to Play
Ss listen to descriptions of countries and throw paper airplanes 
at the correct flash cards. Before class, write the names of the 
countries on small pieces of scrap paper, fold them up and 
place them in a cloth bag.
> Main Activity
Stick the flash cards (P.4.3) up around the classroom (one 
flash card per S, or two if you have a small class).
A S chooses a piece of paper from the cloth bag and gives 
it to you without looking at it. Give clues to the S about that 
country saying for example, “In this country, people speak 
English, you can visit Big Ben and it’s very rainy.” The S must 
ask as many questions as needed to guess which country you’re 
describing by asking, for example, “Is it Egypt?”
When the S guesses correctly, all Ss can throw their airplanes 
at the correct country flash card. The group then walks over 
to where their airplanes are, collects them and stands next to 
that country while a new S gets a turn. Give them five for this 
transition. 
NOTE: if you find that a S is having difficulty guessing, allow 
the other Ss to help. However, once your Ss are used this activity 
they can play the teacher’s role and have their classmates 
guess which country they’re describing.
> Follow-Up
Ask quick questions about the different countries. “In which 
country do people eat maple syrup? Where do they speak 
English and French? Where can you see polar bears?”. Ss 
must run to the country you’re describing and say, “In Canada!”
> Advanced Groups
You can let your Ss take turns being the teacher and giving 
clues to the rest of the group, who will have to guess which 
country they are describing.
5.– ACTIVITY 8: TRAVEL WITH ME SONG (TR#19) (5’)
> How to Play
Get the Ss to stand up in a circle and distribute the flash 
cards of the ten countries mentioned in the song. Introduce the 
activity by saying, “Let’s sing and travel around the world!”. The 
Ss should sing the song and perform the related movements. 
When a country is mentioned, the S holding that flash card

should step forward and turn around in the circle showing their 
classmates the card before returning to their place.
TRAVEL WITH ME SONG
C’mon, c’mon
Come with me 
(make a “come here” motion with your arm by 
stretching it out and then bringing it towards yourself)
Let’s travel the world and see what we can see 
(hold out arms at your sides like an airplane and then 
hold your hand above your eyes as if protecting them 
from the sun and look around)
We can see kangaroos in Australia
And the Statue of Liberty in America
We can see elephants in Africa
And visit the pyramids in Egypt
(chorus)
We can see polar bears in Canada
And visit the Alhambra in Spain
We can visit the Great Wall in China
And the Eiffel Tower in France
(chorus)
We can visit Big Ben in England
And the Taj Mahal in India
So many places for us to see
So come on, come on, travel with me
6.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.

2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and 
do the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
7.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class. 
BONUS
ACTIVITY 4: WHERE ARE YOU FROM?
P.4.3
Italy
> How to Play
Ss must ask and answer questions about where they and their 
classmates are from according to the flash cards they pick up.
> Main Activity
A Ss chooses a Country flash card (P.4.3) and keeps it a secret 
from the rest. The group then asks, “Where are you from?”.

The S should give clues using the following structures:
•	 Where I’m from people speak…
•	 Where I’m from you can see…
•	 Where I’m from people eat…
•	 Where I’m from you can visit…
Ss must guess their classmate’s country by asking for 
example, “Are you from Australia?” to which the S should 
reply, “Yes, I am,” or “No, I am not.” Make sure that every S 
participates either by taking a country or by asking questions. 
As it can take a long time for all Ss to have a go at this activity 
we recommend that you take a note of any Ss that didn’t get 
a go so they can go first the following day.
ACTIVITY 7: COUNTRIES MEMORY LOTTO
P.4.7
South Africa
China
Argentina
P.4.7
P.4.7
> How to Play
For this game, Ss must match the attractions on the Memory 
cards (P.4.7) with the countries on their Bingo boards (P.4.7).
> Main Activity
Give each S one Bingo board and place the Memory cards 
face down in the middle of the table. Introduce the activity by 
saying “Let’s talk about the places we travelled to and what 
we saw there!”
To play, a S turns over a memory card which shows something 
you can see or do in a certain country.
If it is a match the S must say, “I went to South Africa to see 
elephants. It’s a pair. Can I have a counter, please?”
If it is not a match, they must say, “I didn’t go to South Africa 
to see kangaroos; I went to South Africa to see elephants. 
It’s not a pair.”
Adapt the target language (eat, go, see, visit) as needed.
